translations.answer: Maintainers explicitly recommend using contact between two robot links rather than high-gain task. The authors implemented `TaskTwoFramesEquality` and `ContactTwoFramePositions`, which were first reported in a fully-actuated dual-wrist closed chain. PR #218 merged the implementation, Python bindings, and Talos gripper demo. It constrains the relative position of two frames, which can be expressed in this class of loop closure; however, it does not automatically resolve any arbitrary internal passive joints.
translations.applicability: Applicable to rigid closed chains expressed via relative position constraints between two frames; ensure correct geometric matching for target joint types.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and consistent, and there is formal documentation or independent reproducible exact references.
translations.details.attempts.0: The authors implemented and validated `TwoFrames contact`; maintainers recommend recording passive joints in `RobotWrapper` and selecting corresponding M, h, J rows in `InverseDynamicsFormulation` to construct torque-zero equality.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First distinguish between loop-closure constraint and actuation/passive-joint selector; validate whether the contact can maintain relative frame displacement, and separately check the torque=0 equality for passive rows.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Rigid closed chains use the merged path `ContactTwoFramePositions`/`TaskTwoFramesEquality` from PR #218.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: The formulation for arbitrary passive joints has not been implemented in the original thread; do not treat the zero torque-limit hack or PR #218 as a complete solution for a pantograph.
translations.details.environments.0: TSID devel/master 2022-2024; the authors tested `TwoFrames contact` on fully-actuated humanoid wrists and Talos gripper demo; no fixed release available.
translations.details.limits.0: The #218 demo proves a specific closed chain contact, not a general solution for any passive-joint pantograph; a user encountered a segfault in PAL REEM-C TwoFramesEquality after the loop was closed.
translations.details.limits.1: A high-stiffness numerical integration of spring-damper from the maintainers is recommended, but no additional independent card was generated in this thread.
translations.details.outcomes.0: PR #218 merged on 2024-02-02; the maintainers reproduced the minimal code for covariant return and accepted the PR.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The passive-joint selector/equality scheme has no implementation or retesting associated with it.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Should a rigid closed chain of two links be expressed as a task or a contact?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How should arbitrary internal passive joints be expressed after a closed chain is implemented?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: A closed kinematic chain with passive joints can produce false constraints or non-executable torques; verify constraint residual, actuation selector, joint torque, and internal force after real machine testing.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The original TSID formulation only considered the floating base as an unactuated part, and could not declare any arbitrary internal passive joints.
translations.details.symptoms.0: TwoFrames contact works in a fully-actuated closed loop; after pretending pantograph passive joints are torque-limit=0, strange movements occur.
translations.source.locator: TSID #165 maintainers' contact recommendation 1178973756, author's simulation 1181695831; merged PR #218
translations.source.title: TSID two-frame closed chain contact has been merged but arbitrary passive joints still need to be handled separately
translations.title: In TSID, when two robot links form a rigid closed chain, should a high-gain task be used or a contact?
